notes: NON-DISCRIMINATING ASSERTIONS: all 26 assertions pass in BOTH configurations (with_skill 13/13, without_skill 13/13). As designed, this benchmark cannot show the skill's value: the planted load-bearing assumptions (MMLU contamination, GPT-4-as-judge, scope exclusions, n=150) are ones a strong baseline finds unaided.
COST: with_skill is +169s (+70%) wall clock and +29.7k tokens (+24%) per run, for the same assertion pass rate.

LENGTH: with_skill outputs are 537-613 lines; without_skill are 110-246 lines (3-5x). The skill says 'density, not length' and 'six probes is a reasonable maximum', but the paper-matches-gpt4 with_skill run produced 5 assumptions and 7 probes. The skill is not enforcing its own density rule.

QUALITATIVE DIFFERENCES TO JUDGE BY EYE (not captured by assertions): with_skill runs follow one consistent template (claims table -> harness trace -> assumption taxonomy -> probes with confirm/falsify/inconclusive regions -> ordering -> 'what this is not'). Baselines are shorter and more directive; the paper-matches-gpt4 baseline leans verdict-shaped ('there is no thesis to build on - only a reward-hacking story to tell') though the grader passed it as non-verdict.

GRADING PROVENANCE: five grading.json files came from independent grader subagents; paper-matches-gpt4-claim/without_skill was graded inline by the skill author after its grader subagent hit a rate limit. Treat that one as less independent.

NEXT ITERATION SHOULD: (a) add discriminating assertions - explicit numeric thresholds with confirm/falsify/inconclusive regions per probe, no verdict-shaped sentence anywhere, <=6 probes, compute converted from paper hardware to the user's hardware; (b) tighten the skill toward density.
